title: Gift Wrap Station Ideas: One Spot for Paper, Tape and Scissors (Finally)
description: Stop buying tape every December. Set up an ADHD-friendly gift wrap station in one bin, closet door or cart, plus 8 Amazon finds that keep it together.
intro:
It's 10 p.m. on December 23rd. You have the gifts. You have three rolls of wrapping paper (one is from 2019 and has a tear down the middle). What you don't have: tape. Or scissors. Or the gift tags you know you bought.

So you buy more tape. And next year it happens again, because the tape you bought is now in the junk drawer, the car and somebody's craft box.

A gift wrap station fixes this. Not a Pinterest-perfect wrapping room. One spot where every wrapping thing lives together, so wrapping a gift is one trip instead of a scavenger hunt. Here's how to set it up in an afternoon (or a few 15-minute chunks), plus eight Amazon finds that make it easy to keep up with.

sections.heading: Round up everything first
sections.body:
Set a timer for 15 minutes and walk the house with a laundry basket. Grab every roll, gift bag, tissue sheet, bow, ribbon, tag, tape and pair of scissors you can find.

Don't sort while you walk. Collect, then dump it all on the floor in one room. Seeing it all in one pile is the moment you realize you own 14 gift bags and zero tape. That's useful information.

sections.heading: Keep less than you think
sections.body:
Now do a fast edit. Toss crumpled tissue, ribbon that's knotted into a ball and wrapping paper rolls with only a sad foot left. Keep:

- 3 to 5 rolls of paper you actually like
- A small stack of gift bags in a few sizes
- One bag of tissue paper
- Ribbon or bows you'll use this year

Fewer choices means faster wrapping. When you have 11 papers, you stand there deciding. When you have 4, you grab one and go.

sections.heading: Pick a station spot that matches your space
sections.body:
There's no one right setup. Choose the one you can see and reach:

- **Under the bed:** a long, flat bin holds rolls lying down and slides out when you need it.
- **Back of a closet door:** an over-the-door organizer holds rolls upright and supplies in pockets.
- **A rolling cart:** wheel it to the couch, wrap during a show, wheel it back.
- **One upright bin in a closet:** rolls stand up like umbrellas, supplies in a caddy beside it.

If you live in a small space, the under-bed bin or the door are your friends.

sections.heading: Give the small stuff a caddy
sections.body:
Rolls are easy. Small stuff is where the chaos lives. Put tape, scissors, tags, a pen and a few bows in one handled caddy. When you wrap, you carry the whole caddy to the gift. When you're done, everything goes back in the caddy.

Bonus move: buy a second pair of scissors that lives *only* in the caddy. Tie a ribbon on them so everyone knows they're the wrapping scissors.

sections.heading: Wrap as gifts arrive
sections.body:
The biggest wrapping stress is doing it all in one night. Try this instead: when a gift arrives, wrap it that day, or at least that week. Add a tag right away so you don't end up with a pile of mystery boxes.

If wrapping in the moment is too much, put unwrapped gifts in one bin next to the station with a sticky note of who they're for. Then wrap three at a time while you watch something.

sections.heading: Make it a year-round station
sections.body: Birthdays, baby showers and teacher gifts happen all year. Keep a few solid-color papers and plain bags in the station so it works in June, too. A station you use all year is a station you remember exists.

outro:
A gift wrap station isn't about being crafty. It's about never buying tape on December 23rd again. One spot, a few rolls you like and a caddy for the small stuff is all it takes.

If the rest of your holiday plan could use the same one-spot idea, *The Messy Brain Home Reset* walks you through the house one small zone at a time.
